sub_scenario.family: physical constraint versus sustained work commitment
sub_scenario.one_line: warehouse operations trainer: poor fit as currently formatted

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the floor-walk plan and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The onboarding roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Walking warehouse audits, hours of them, never bother my knee at all.
So movement is fine.
Movement is fine; it is static standing that bites.
Someone new shadowed me in the training floor this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the intake weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
After I led two full days of floor demonstrations on the concrete without sit breaks, my knee swelled overnight and I limped through the next morning's session.
Static standing on concrete is the trigger?
Documented twice now. Same pattern both times.
A single standing training day with an evening to recover is completely manageable.
One day is inside the envelope.
Comfortably inside it.
I archived last cycle's notes on the onboarding roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My physiotherapist capped my continuous standing at ninety minutes per stretch through flare season.
A written cap.
Written into my occupational health file, even.
A vendor call about the floor-walk plan ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the training floor checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the intake weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the onboarding roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The five-day onboarding intake is formatted as eight-hour standing floor-walks with no seated modules; the remodel removed the classroom benches entirely.
Five consecutive all-standing days.
On concrete, with nowhere to sit even between groups.
I sketched next week's plan for the intake weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the floor-walk plan updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Flare season for me runs exactly across the spring intake calendar.
The timing could not be worse.
It never can, apparently.
I compared two options for the onboarding roster tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the training floor handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
They are assigning trainers for the five-day onboarding intake. Is that week, as currently formatted, a fit for me?
